article_content:
A recent social media post has claimed that vaccinating all 3.2 million Japanese high school students would result in 50 deaths or cases of severe adverse side effects. This statement raises concerns about vaccine safety and the risks associated with large-scale immunization campaigns targeting young people. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine the available data, the context of vaccine administration in Japan, and the known rates of severe adverse reactions among adolescents.

Vaccines, including those developed for COVID-19, undergo rigorous safety testing before being approved for use in any population. In Japan, as in other countries, health authorities closely monitor vaccine safety through adverse event reporting systems. Severe adverse side effects from vaccines—such as anaphylaxis, myocarditis, or death—are rare, but they do occur and are subject to detailed investigation.

The claim in question implies that among 3.2 million vaccinated high school students, approximately 50 would die or experience severe side effects. To evaluate this, we need to consider the actual rates of such events reported in Japan and internationally. For mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, which have been the primary vaccines used among adolescents, the rate of severe adverse reactions such as myocarditis has been estimated to be around 1-5 cases per 100,000 doses in young males, with even lower rates in females. Deaths directly attributable to the vaccine in this age group are exceedingly rare, with most investigations finding no causal link.

Applying even the higher end of the myocarditis rate (5 per 100,000) to 3.2 million students would result in an estimated 160 cases of myocarditis. However, most myocarditis cases reported after vaccination are mild and resolve with treatment. The rate of fatal outcomes or long-term severe disability from vaccine-induced myocarditis in adolescents is extremely low—likely well below 1 in a million.

Other severe adverse events, such as anaphylaxis, occur at a rate of approximately 2-5 cases per million doses. When considering all severe side effects (including anaphylaxis, myocarditis, and other rare reactions), the combined rate remains below 10 per million doses for adolescents. This suggests that among 3.2 million students, the expected number of severe adverse reactions would likely be in the range of 30-32 cases, with deaths being extremely rare, possibly one or none.

It is also important to note that the risks of severe outcomes from COVID-19 itself, though lower for teenagers than older adults, are not zero. Vaccination provides significant protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and complications.

In summary, the claim that 50 Japanese high school students would die or suffer severe adverse side effects if all were vaccinated overstates the known risks based on current data. While some cases of severe side effects may occur, the number is likely lower than suggested, and fatal outcomes are exceedingly rare. Vaccine safety continues to be monitored, and the benefits of vaccination in preventing COVID-19 complications outweigh the risks of rare adverse events. It is crucial for public discussions to be informed by accurate data and ongoing scientific review.

A recent social media post has sparked concern by claiming that epinephrine, the drug commonly used to treat anaphylactic attacks, is not stocked nationwide and that adrenaline is available instead. This claim raises important questions about the availability of life-saving medications and the terminology used in medical practice. Here, we take a closer look at the facts behind these statements to provide a clear understanding for the public.

Epinephrine and adrenaline are, in fact, two names for the same medication. Epinephrine is the term predominantly used in the United States and by the World Health Organization, while adrenaline is commonly used in the United Kingdom and many other countries. Both refer to the same chemical compound, which acts quickly to reverse severe allergic reactions by constricting blood vessels, opening airways, and reducing swelling. Therefore, the suggestion that adrenaline is available "instead" of epinephrine is misleading; they are not separate drugs but rather different names for the same treatment.

The next point in the post—that epinephrine is "not stocked nationwide"—requires careful examination. Epinephrine is considered an essential medication and is routinely stocked in hospitals, ambulances, and pharmacies, especially in the form of auto-injectors such as EpiPen. These devices are crucial for immediate treatment of anaphylaxis outside medical settings. However, in recent years, there have been periodic reports of shortages and supply issues with epinephrine auto-injectors, usually due to manufacturing delays, increased demand, or regulatory challenges. These shortages have sometimes led to difficulties for patients in obtaining their prescribed auto-injectors, but they have not resulted in a nationwide absence of the medication itself.

It is important to distinguish between the availability of epinephrine in auto-injector form versus other formulations. While auto-injectors are designed for self-administration and rapid response, healthcare providers have access to epinephrine in ampoules and vials for injection in emergency settings. Hospitals and emergency services stock epinephrine in various forms, ensuring that it is available for life-threatening allergic reactions. Pharmacies may occasionally experience local shortages of auto-injectors, but this does not equate to a complete lack of epinephrine nationwide.

Additionally, regulatory agencies and pharmaceutical companies have taken steps to mitigate supply disruptions, including allowing the use of alternative brands or extending expiration dates of existing stock in times of shortage. Public health authorities closely monitor the supply of essential medicines like epinephrine to prevent gaps in availability.

In summary, the social media post conflates terminology and overstates the issue regarding medication availability. Adrenaline and epinephrine are the same drug, not alternatives. While there have been instances of supply challenges with epinephrine auto-injectors, epinephrine itself remains a well-stocked, essential medication used to treat anaphylactic attacks across the country. The public is encouraged to consult healthcare professionals for accurate information and to check with pharmacies regarding the availability of specific formulations.

Šis apgalvojums uzdara jautājumus par medikamentu pieejamību un medicīnas prakses terminoloģiju. Šeit mēs pārskatām faktu, lai sniegtu skaidru informāciju sabiedrībai.

Epinefrīns un adrenalīns patiesībā ir divi nosaukumi vienam un tam pašam medicīniskajam līdzeklim. Epinefrīns tiek izmantots galvenokārt ASV un Pasaules Veselības Organizācijas (PVO) kontekstā, savukārt adrenalīns ir parasti izmantots ASV un daudzās citas valstīs. Abi atsauce uz to pašu ķīmisko savienojumu, kas ātri iedarbojas, lai atvērtu smagus alerģiskus reakcijas, samazinot asinsvadu izplatību un samazinot svelmi. Tāpēc apgalvojums, ka adrenalīns tiek izmantots "vietā" epinefrīna, ir neprecīzs; tie nav atsevišķi līdzekļi, bet gan dažādi nosaukumi vienam un tam pašam ārstēšanas veidam.

Ziņojuma nākamais punkts – ka epinefrīns ir "nav pieejams visā valstī" – prasa uzmanīgu pārskatīšanu. Epinefrīns tiek uzskatīts par būtisku medicīnisku līdzekli un ir parastāk pieejams slimnīcās, ambulancēs un apotekās, īpaši automātiskos injektoros, piemēram, EpiPen. Šie ierīces ir svarīgi ārpus medicīnas iestāžu apstākļos, lai sniegtu tūlītēju anafilaktiskās reakcijas ārstēšanu. Tomēr pēdējos gados ir periodiski ziņots par epinefrīna automātisko injektoru trūkumiem un piegādes problēmām, galvenokārt dēļ ražošanas aizkavēšanās, palielināta pieprasījuma vai regulatīvām izpratnēm. Šie trūkumi dažkārt izraisījuši grūtības pacientiem, lai iegūstu iepirkto automātisko injektoru, tomēr nevienu reizi nav radies vispārējs epinefrīna trūkums.

Svarīgi atšķirt epinefrīna pieejamību automātiskos injektoros no citām formām. Šie ierīces ir paredzēti pašu izmantošanai un ātru reakcijas nodrošināšanai, tomēr medicīnas darbinieki var izmantot epinefrīnu ampulēs un vialās injekcijām ārkārtas apstākļos. Slimnīcas un ārsta dienestu iestādes saglabā epinefrīnu dažādās formās, nodrošinot tās pieejamību dzīvošanas apdraudējošām alerģiskām reakcijām. Apotekas var reizēm saskarties ar vietējiem automātisko injektoru trūkumiem, taču tas nezīmējas par vispārēju epinefrīna trūkumu valstī.

Līdz ar to, regulatīvās iestādes un farmaceitiskās uzņēmumi ir veikuši pasākumus, lai samazinātu piegādes traucējumus, ieviešot alternatīvu zīmolu izmantošanu vai izmantojot esošās zāļu pārbaudes datu pārtraukumu laikā. Publiskās veselības iestādes uzrauga būtisko zāļu piegādi, piemēram, epinefrīnu, lai izvairītos no piegādes plaisām.

Kopsavilkumā, sociālās medijas ziņojums sakrīt terminoloģijas un pārspēj uztraukumu par zāļu pieejamības jautājumu. Adrenalīns un epinefrīns ir viens un tas pats līdzeklis, nevis alternatīvi. Visbiežāk ir bijuši epinefrīna automātisko injektoru piegādes problēmas, taču epinefrīns pats paliek būtisks, pieejams zāļu veids, kas tiek izmantots anafilaktisku uzbrukumu ārstēšanai visā valstī. Publikai ieteicams konsultēties ar medicīnas darbiniekiem, lai iegūtu precīzu informāciju un pārbaudīt apotekas, lai noskaidrotu konkrēto formātu pieejamību.

A claim circulating on social media asserts that the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has admitted there is “no Covid-19.” This allegation has garnered attention and sparked confusion, especially among those questioning the validity of the Covid-19 pandemic and the associated public health response. A careful examination of the claim, the context, and the CDC’s actual communications reveals that this statement is false and misinterprets both scientific and public health information.

Covid-19, caused by the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, was first identified in late 2019 and rapidly spread worldwide. The CDC, along with the World Health Organization (WHO) and multiple health agencies, has played a central role in tracking cases, developing testing protocols, and offering guidance on prevention and treatment. The pandemic has resulted in millions of deaths and has had profound social and economic impacts globally.

The core of the social media claim centers on the idea that the CDC itself has acknowledged Covid-19 does not exist. This assertion is usually based on a misreading or deliberate distortion of CDC documents or statements. One common source of confusion is the transition from one type of Covid-19 test to another. For example, in 2021, the CDC announced it would withdraw its request for Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for a specific polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test for detecting SARS-CoV-2. Some individuals misinterpreted this technical update as evidence that the virus was never isolated or that Covid-19 is not real.

In reality, the CDC’s decision to retire a particular test was based on the availability of newer tests that could simultaneously differentiate between SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses, such as influenza. The original PCR test was developed early in the pandemic and served its purpose, but advances in diagnostics rendered it less necessary. At no point did the CDC state or imply that SARS-CoV-2 does not exist or that Covid-19 is not a real disease.

Additionally, the CDC has published extensive information about the isolation, genetic sequencing, and characterization of SARS-CoV-2. The agency maintains resources on Covid-19 case numbers, hospitalizations, deaths, and vaccine guidance. The CDC’s ongoing updates and public communications continue to affirm the reality of the virus and the disease it causes.

The scientific consensus, supported by research institutions around the world, confirms that Covid-19 is a real and significant infectious disease. Claims to the contrary often stem from misinformation, misunderstanding of scientific processes, or deliberate attempts to undermine public health messaging.

In summary, the allegation that the CDC has admitted there is “no Covid-19” is false. The CDC has never made such a statement, and all available evidence supports the existence and impact of Covid-19. As with all public health information, it is important to rely on credible sources and verified data when evaluating claims about the pandemic.

एक सामाजिक मीडिया पर घूम रहे दावे के अनुसार, संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के रोग नियंत्रण और रोग प्रतिरोध विभाग (CDC) ने "कोविड-19 नहीं है" के बारे में स्वीकृति दी है। इस दावे के ध्यान आकर्षण और गड़बड़ी के बीच बहस उत्पन्न कर दिया है, विशेष रूप से वे लोग जो कोविड-19 महामारी और संबंधित सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य प्रतिक्रिया के वैधता के बारे में संदेह कर रहे हैं। दावे के विवरण, संदर्भ और CDC के वास्तविक संचार की एक ध्यान से जांच करने से पता चलता है कि यह कथन गलत है और वैज्ञानिक और सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य जानकारी के गलत अर्थ देता है।

कोविड-19, नए कोरोनावायरस SARS-CoV-2 द्वारा कारण होता है, जो वर्ष 2019 के अंत में पहली बार पहचाना गया था और तेजी से वैश्विक स्तर पर फैल गया। CDC, विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन (WHO) और कई स्वास्थ्य एजेंसियों द्वारा मामलों के ट्रैक करने, टेस्टिंग प्रोटोकॉल विकसित करने और रोकथाम और उपचार के निर्देश देने में मुख्य भूमिका निभाई गई। महामारी ने दुनिया भर में करोड़ों मौतों के साथ गहरे सामाजिक और आर्थिक प्रभाव डाले हैं।

सामाजिक मीडिया के दावे के केंद्र में यह विचार है कि CDC ने कोविड-19 के अस्तित्व के बारे में स्वीकृति दी है। इस दावे के आधार आमतौर पर CDC दस्तावेज या कथनों के गलत अर्थ अथवा निश्चित रूप से विकृत अर्थ देते हैं। एक सामान्य भ्रम के अंतर्गत एक प्रकार के कोविड-19 टेस्ट से दूसरे प्रकार के टेस्ट के परिवर्तन के बारे में होता है। उदाहरण के लिए, 2021 में CDC ने एक विशिष्ट पॉलिमरेज चैन रिएक्शन (PCR) टेस्ट के लिए आपातकालीन उपयोग प्रमाणीकरण (EUA) के अनुरोध को वापस लेने की घोषणा की। कुछ व्यक्ति इस तकनीकी अपडेट को वायरस कभी अलग किए बिना या कोविड-19 के अस्तित्व के बारे में गलत अर्थ देते हैं।

वास्तविकता में, CDC के एक विशिष्ट टेस्ट के बाहर जाने का निर्णय नए टेस्ट की उपलब्धता पर आधारित था, जो एक साथ SARS-CoV-2 और अन्य श्वसन वायरस जैसे इंफ्लूएंजा के बीच अंतर कर सकते थे। आरंभिक PCR टेस्ट पीड़ित लोगों के लिए उपयोगी था, लेकिन नए निदान तकनीकों के कारण इसकी आवश्यकता कम हो गई। कोई भी समय बिंदु जब CDC ने या इशारा किया कि SARS-CoV-2 नहीं है या कोविड-19 एक वास्तविक बीमारी नहीं है।

साथ ही, CDC ने SARS-CoV-2 के अलग करने, जीनेटिक सीक्वेंसिंग और वर्गीकरण के बारे में विस्तृत जानकारी प्रकाशित की है। एजेंसी के संसाधन कोविड-19 मामलों की संख्या, अस्पतालों में भर्ती, मृत्यु और टीका निर्देश के बारे में रखे गए हैं। CDC के निरंतर अपडेट और सार्वजनिक संचार वायरस और इसके कारण बीमारी के वास्तविकता की पुष्टि करते रहे हैं।

वैज्ञानिक सहमति, विश्व के अनेक अनुसंधान संस्थानों द्वारा समर्थित, कोविड-19 के वास्तविक और महत्वपूर्ण संक्रामक बीमारी के बारे में पुष्टि करती है। इसके विपरीत दावे अक्सर गलत जानकारी, वैज्ञानिक प्रक्रियाओं के गलत अर्थ या जन स्वास्थ्य संदेश को नीचे लाने के लिए निश्चित प्रयासों से उत्पन्न होते हैं।

संक्षेप में, CDC ने "कोविड-19 नहीं है" के बारे में स्वीकृति देने के दावे गलत है। CDC ने ऐसा कोई बयान नहीं दिया है, और सभी उपलब्ध सबूत कोविड-19 के अस्तित्व और इसके प्रभाव के समर्थन करते हैं। महामारी के बारे में कथन के आकलन के लिए, सभी सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य जानकारी के लिए विश्वसनीय स्रोत और सत्यापित डेटा पर निर्भर करना महत्वपूर्ण है।
article_summary: SNSで広まった「CDCがコロナウイルス感染症（COVID-19）を否定した」という主張は誤情報であり、CDCはウイルスの存在を否定したことはない。2021年に特定のPCR検査を廃止したのは、より正確な検査法への移行であり、ウイルスの存在を否定するものではない。CDCはウイルスの遺伝子配列や感染症の実態を明確に発表しており、科学的根拠に基づく情報が提供されている。
